cause: The square model input includes letterbox padding outside the camera field of view. Displaying its entire generated square exposes generated/stale padding as a horizontal band.

attachment_layout.measurement: approximate visual coordinates in the native attachment; no image copied into the project or remote service
attachment_layout.limitation: A still screenshot supports the padding-location diagnosis but cannot itself prove video freezing.

implementation.capture: VideoFrame/ImageBitmap worker and main fallback report the actual snapshot content rectangle
implementation.presentation: map the same frame rectangle into each generated resolution; one drawImage pass displays the whole camera field and omits only letterbox padding
implementation.normalization: capture pixels converted to [0,1] before storing with frame ID

replay.source: public frames only, synthetic 960x720 camera at 30fps, actual VideoFrame worker + existing RTX5090 + browser presentation; no user camera accessed
replay.model: same existing FLUX.2 Klein / FluxRT, motion-priority, fast, two steps, no interpolation
replay.comparison: ABBA isolates presentation rect=null (uncropped) versus actual recorded contentRect; encoding and model settings identical

limitations: Only padding is excluded; no face/body garment masking, pasting, or invented camera content added.
This fixes the geometry error demonstrated by the horizontal band, not all generative identity/garment errors inside the camera area.
80 public replay frames do not establish human quality or network reliability.
Existing optional interpolation, cache policy and model configuration remain unchanged.
